subject: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@apexhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@apexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Auditors asked us for a concise narrative and diagrams that show how Redwood separates control plane, data plane, and tenant data for both Dedicated and Private deployment models. Specifically they want:

- Network diagram(s) that clearly label control plane endpoints, management interfaces, and tenant compute zones (for both Dedicated and on-prem Private options).
- A short paragraph (1-2 pages) describing how tenant isolation is enforced and where KMS/HSM boundaries are.
- Mapping to SIG and CAIQ questions that are commonly checked in SOC 2 audits (network segregation, egress controls, control plane access controls).

Can you provide a deliverable we can hand straight to the auditor (PDF + diagrams) by COB Monday? We also need a one-page executive summary for our security leadership.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Morgan
Lead, Security & Compliance
Apex Health

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@apexhealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attaching an initial narrative (redwood_control_surface_narrative_v1.docx) and a diagram pack (link below) that separates the control plane from the data plane for both Dedicated and Private deployments. Highlights in the doc:

- Control plane ownership: Redwood-managed control plane for Hosted & Dedicated (with VPC peering options); customer-managed control plane option for air-gapped Private.
- Data plane tenancy: per-tenant compute domains, enforced by networking + namespace isolation at the runtime layer.
- KMS boundary: we call out where customer-managed KMS integrates (customer key wrap) for Private and Dedicated with CMKs stored in their KMS.

Drive link (diagram assets): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBx-example-diagrams

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll update the diagram to show per-tenant egress policing and default-deny rules (tomorrow).
2) Kimberly will add CAIQ/SIG mapping rows for the network and control plane questions.
3) I’ll produce the 1-page exec summary (draft by EOD Mon).

Can we do a 30-min sync on Monday morning to walk the auditor through the control plane flows? I can invite Jonas from infra for the deep-dive.

–Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_control_surface_narrative_v1.docx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@apexhealth.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation

Adding a few details for the auditor pack:

- Segmentation matrix: attached (segmentation_matrix_apex.csv) with rows for control plane endpoints, tenant compute ranges, and allowed egress destinations.
- CAIQ mapping: I started a one-page mapping (soc2_sig_ca iq_mapping_onepager.pdf) that ties common CAIQ fields (e.g., NET-1, NET-3, INF-5) and SIG network controls to our architecture statements.
- Cross-tenant protections: runtime enforces memory & KV cache separation by namespace; network layer enforces SG-level deny-by-default with explicit outbound proxies for telemetry.
- Audit artifacts: recommended artifacts we can supply: flow logs for sample tenant, KMS access logs (redacted), and control plane RBAC roster for the audit window.

I’ll iterate the diagram to label the management plane interfaces (SSH/pssh/ops API) and call out the firewall ACLs that block tenant-to-tenant lateral movement.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: segmentation_matrix_apex.csv, soc2_sig_ca iq_mapping_onepager.pdf

From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@apexhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Ben Cho <ben.cho@apexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation

Thanks Karthik and Kimberly — this is exactly the right direction. A few clarifying asks from the auditor:

1) Can you explicitly annotate the network diagram with labels for the control plane public endpoints vs private management endpoints (they want to see which endpoints are reachable from the internet vs via peering/VPN).
2) For the Private (on-prem / air-gapped) option, the auditor wants a short blurb that states who is responsible for patching control-plane components and how security updates are distributed.
3) SIG callouts: they specifically requested the SIG question ids for control-plane authentication and for egress filtering. Can you put those ids into the mapping doc (we need the exact field ids).

Also — if possible, can you provide a single-page PDF (executive_summary_audit_ready.pdf) that contains the one-paragraph isolation narrative, two diagrams (high-level: control/data plane split + per-tenant egress), and an explicit list of artifacts we can hand the auditor in the live session? If you can get that to us by COB Monday it will keep the audit on schedule.

Best,
Alice

Date: 2026-08-24T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Control surface narrative for SOC 2 / SIG - Dedicated & Private isolation

Alice —

Attached: final diagram set (redwood_dedicated_private_network_diagram_v2.png) and a one-page executive summary (executive_summary_audit_ready.pdf). Items called out in the summary:

- Control plane endpoints: public API endpoints (load-balanced, WAF-protected) are marked in red; private management endpoints (ops VPN / peered control plane) marked in blue.
- Private deployment responsibilities: customer-owned control plane for air-gapped Private; we provide signed binary update artifacts and an update manifest that customers pull via an approved channel. We list patching responsibilities & recommended cadence in the appendix.
- SIG/CAIQ mapping: we mapped SIG v2024 question ids for authentication (SIG-AUTH-2, SIG-AUTH-4) and for egress filtering (SIG-NET-1, SIG-NET-3) in the attached mapping PDF.
- Audit artifacts we can hand over on request: flow logs for a sample tenant range (redacted), KMS access audit trail (redacted timestamps), control plane RBAC snapshot for the audit date, and the segmentation_matrix_apex.csv.

Action items & timeline:
1) Deliver final auditor pack (this email attachments + mapping PDF) — DONE (attached).
2) Provide sample flow logs and KMS audit extracts — I’ll coordinate with Jonas to deliver redacted extracts by 2026-08-27.
3) 30-min walkthrough with auditor — I’m available Monday 09:00-11:30 PT; Jonas will cover operational controls.

If you need any further annotation (auditors often ask for explicit ACL lines or CIDR ranges) I can add a text layer to the PNG and export a printer-ready PDF.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_private_network_diagram_v2.png, executive_summary_audit_ready.pdf
